# Strong at 70: how it works {: .nobreak}

<div class="chang" markdown="1">
<div class="who">Chang Yin</div>

I'm Chang. AI character. Twelve weeks, one program, done properly. Build the leg, arm and grip strength daily life asks for: chairs, stairs, the floor, the groceries.

A little more, slowly. That's the whole method.
</div>


**Who it's for.** Adults 60+ who can stand from a chair (hands allowed) and want structured strength training at home. Every level from Rebuild to Iron.

<div class="box stop" markdown="1">
<span class="label">Ask your doctor first if:</span> Chest pain or unusual breathlessness with activity, fainting, recent surgery or fracture, a heart or kidney condition with symptoms, or a new hip or knee (follow your surgeon's precautions; kneeling may be off-limits).
</div>


**What you need.** Sturdy chair against a wall, kitchen counter, stairs with a rail, water jugs or grocery bags, a folded towel. Optional: the Strong Years band kit.

<div class="box stop" markdown="1">
<span class="label">Every day:</span> Stop if you feel chest pain or pressure, dizziness, unusual shortness of breath, or sharp pain. Chest pain, face drooping, arm weakness or trouble speaking? Call 911 now. Pain rule (E41): Mild discomfort up to 3 out of 10 is okay if it settles by tomorrow. Sharper, or worse the next day: back off and ask your doctor or physical therapist.
</div>




## Your week

Mon: program session A · Tue: mobility · Wed: balance · Thu: program session B · Fri: breath + qigong · Sat: walk-and-talk · Sun: rest + stretch. Program sessions are marked in **bold** in the plan; the other days use your Strong Years Daily Practice sessions (DP numbers).

## How it progresses

Three 4-week phases: **Foundation** (weeks 1–4, A1/B1), **Build** (weeks 5–8, A2/B2) and **Strengthen** (weeks 9–12, A3/B3).

| Week in each phase | Rule |
|---|---|
| 1st | Doses as written in the session. Learn the moves. Stop each set with one or two good reps left in the tank. |
| 2nd | Add 1–2 reps per set (never past 12). Holds up 5 seconds (never past 30). |
| 3rd | Where every rep felt easy two sessions in a row, use the Harder version or a heavier jug. Otherwise repeat week 2. |
| 4th (easy week) | Easy week: same moves, one set fewer. Then do your checkpoint at the weekend. |

**Levels.** Every session has four versions: Rebuild (chair-based), Steady, Strong and Iron. Move up only when every rep felt easy two sessions in a row. Move down any day. **Advanced** doses are never a starting point.

<div class="box stop" markdown="1">
<span class="label">Red flags:</span> Not for exercise. For your doctor, today: chest pain or pressure; fainting; sudden weakness or numbness in the face, arm or leg; trouble speaking; a sudden severe headache; new confusion; one calf that is swollen, red and painful; a hot, swollen joint; night pain that wakes you and doesn't change with position; fever with back pain; loss of bladder or bowel control or numbness in the saddle area; a fall where you hit your head (especially on blood thinners). Chest pain, face drooping, arm weakness or trouble speaking? Call 911 now.
</div>




# Your checkpoints

Start, then the end of weeks 4, 8 and 12. Same chair, same shoes, same time of day. These are fitness checks from published research, **not medical tests**.

### 0:35–1:00 · Ankle pumps

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>0:35</td><td>Chang</td><td>Sit tall. Chair against the wall.</td><td>Ankle pumps</td></tr>
<tr><td>0:42</td><td>Chang</td><td>Point your toes away, then pull them toward you. That's one pump.</td><td>Easier: Smaller movements</td></tr>
<tr><td>0:46</td><td>Chang</td><td>Big, slow movements.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>0:50</td><td>Chang</td><td>Feel your calves work.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>0:54</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe slowly.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Big, slow movements. Feel your calves work. **Easier:** Smaller movements. **Harder:** Lift one foot off the floor while you circle.

**Safety callouts:** Great before you stand up from sitting or lying. Sit a moment before you stand, then stand slowly while holding something steady.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 1:00–1:40 · March

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>1:00</td><td>Chang</td><td>Stand slowly. Hand on the counter.</td><td>March</td></tr>
<tr><td>1:19</td><td>Chang</td><td>March. Easy rhythm. Breathe steady.</td><td>Easier: Sit and march</td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Stand tall. Knee up, foot down softly. **Easier:** Sit and do the seated march. **Harder:** Lift knees higher, march faster, or let one hand hover above the counter.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 1:40–2:00 · Shoulder rolls

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>1:40</td><td>Chang</td><td>Sit tall. Chair against the wall.</td><td>Shoulder rolls</td></tr>
<tr><td>1:46</td><td>Chang</td><td>Lift your shoulders up toward your ears.</td><td>Easier: Just shrug and let go</td></tr>
<tr><td>1:49</td><td>Chang</td><td>Big, slow circles, backward.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>1:52</td><td>Chang</td><td>Let your arms hang heavy.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>1:55</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe in as you lift, out as you roll down.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Big, slow circles, backward. Let your arms hang heavy. **Easier:** Just shrug up and let go. **Harder:** Add arm circles: small circles out to the sides, forward and back.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 2:00–3:50 · Legs

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>2:00</td><td>Chang</td><td>Hand on the counter. Chair behind you.</td><td>Legs</td></tr>
<tr><td>2:20</td><td>Chang</td><td>Cross your arms over your chest, or rest your hands on your thighs.</td><td>Easier: Higher seat, hands on thighs</td></tr>
<tr><td>2:38</td><td>Chang</td><td>Nose over toes.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>2:49</td><td>Chang</td><td>One... two... breathe out... three... slow down... four.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>2:55</td><td>Chang</td><td>Knees point the same way as your toes. Don't let them cave inward.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>3:13</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe out as you stand. Breathe in as you sit.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Nose over toes. Knees point the same way as your toes. Don't let them cave inward. Sit down slow. Two or three seconds. **Easier:** Put a firm cushion or folded blanket on the seat to make it higher, or push up with your hands on your thighs or on chair arms. **Harder:** Arms crossed, lower for a slow count of three, and pause one second just above the seat before touching down. Later: hold a gallon jug of water at your chest.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 3:50–5:20 · Push

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>3:50</td><td>Chang</td><td>Wall in front of you or behind you. Chair nearby.</td><td>Push</td></tr>
<tr><td>4:07</td><td>Chang</td><td>Bend your elbows and bring your chest toward the wall.</td><td>Easier: Closer to wall, half range</td></tr>
<tr><td>4:21</td><td>Chang</td><td>Body in one straight line, head to heels.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>4:30</td><td>Chang</td><td>One... two... breathe out... three... slow down... four.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>4:36</td><td>Chang</td><td>Chest to the wall, not your chin.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>4:50</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe out as you push away.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Body in one straight line, head to heels. Chest to the wall, not your chin. **Easier:** Stand closer to the wall and move only halfway. **Harder:** Step your feet farther back. When 15 are easy, move to counter push-ups.

**Safety callouts:** Wrist pain? Make fists or hold the counter edge instead of flat palms.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 5:20–6:40 · Suitcase lift

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>5:20</td><td>Chang</td><td>Hand on the counter. Chair behind you.</td><td>Suitcase lift</td></tr>
<tr><td>5:35</td><td>Chang</td><td>Push your hips back with a long back and bend your knees a little.</td><td>Easier: Lighter jug, higher surface</td></tr>
<tr><td>5:48</td><td>Chang</td><td>Hips back. Long back.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>5:56</td><td>Chang</td><td>One... two... breathe out... three... slow down... four.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>6:01</td><td>Chang</td><td>Don't lean toward the jug. Stay square.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>6:14</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe out as you stand.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Hips back. Long back. Don't lean toward the jug. Stay square. **Easier:** A lighter jug, and lift it from a higher surface like the counter's edge of a table. **Harder:** A heavier bag, or lift from the bottom step instead of the chair.

**Safety callouts:** Osteoporosis: this is the safe bending pattern. Keep the back long, never curl. Osteoporosis or a past spine fracture: long back always, never round to reach.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 6:40–7:30 · Heel raises

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>6:40</td><td>Chang</td><td>Hand on the counter. Chair behind you.</td><td>Heel raises</td></tr>
<tr><td>6:51</td><td>Chang</td><td>Rise up onto the balls of your feet, as high as is comfortable.</td><td>Easier: Seated, or rise halfway</td></tr>
<tr><td>6:59</td><td>Chang</td><td>Tall like someone is pulling a string on top of your head.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>7:02</td><td>Chang</td><td>One... two... breathe out... three... slow down... four.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>7:07</td><td>Chang</td><td>Weight over the big toe and second toe, not rolling out.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>7:15</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe out as you rise.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Tall like someone is pulling a string on top of your head. Weight over the big toe and second toe, not rolling out. **Easier:** Sit in your chair and raise your heels from there, or hold the counter with both hands and rise only halfway. **Harder:** One hand on the counter. Later: one leg at a time, with both hands on the counter.

**Safety callouts:** Calf cramps are common at first. Stretch and walk them out. One calf that is swollen, red and painful is not a cramp: that is for your doctor, today.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 7:30–8:50 · Floor practice

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>7:30</td><td>Chang</td><td>Chair or sofa beside you. Towel down. Someone else home.</td><td>Floor practice</td></tr>
<tr><td>7:54</td><td>Chang</td><td>Step back, lower one knee to the towel. Hands on the chair.</td><td>Easier: Half-kneel only, or chair stands</td></tr>
<tr><td>8:15</td><td>Chang</td><td>Push up through the front foot. Breathe out. Stand still a moment.</td><td>Only with a sturdy chair and someone home</td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Hands on the chair the whole time. Slow down. Up is a push, not a jump. **Easier:** Only the first step: lower into a half-kneel on the towel and come back up, holding the chair. Or skip the floor and do sit-to-stands. **Harder:** Iron: from kneeling, sit down onto the floor beside the chair, then roll to your knees and rise with the chair. Only with someone home.

**Safety callouts:** Only try the floor with a sturdy chair or sofa next to you and someone home. Recent hip or knee replacement, or severe knee arthritis: follow your surgeon's or physical therapist's guidance first. New knee? Kneeling may not be allowed yet. Ask your surgeon. Sit a moment before you stand, then stand slowly while holding something steady.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 8:50–9:30 · Calf stretch

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>8:50</td><td>Chang</td><td>Hand on the counter. Chair behind you.</td><td>Calf stretch</td></tr>
<tr><td>8:59</td><td>Chang</td><td>Bend the front knee and lean gently toward the wall until you feel a stretch in the back calf.</td><td>Easier: Smaller step back</td></tr>
<tr><td>9:05</td><td>Chang</td><td>Back heel stays down.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>9:12</td><td>Chang</td><td>Toes point forward.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>9:18</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe slowly through the stretch.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Back heel stays down. Toes point forward. **Easier:** Smaller step back. **Harder:** Bigger step back, or bend the back knee slightly to reach the lower calf.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 9:30–10:10 · Cyclic sighing

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>9:30</td><td>Chang</td><td>Sit. Two sniffs in through the nose. One long sigh out.</td><td>Cyclic sighing</td></tr>
<tr><td>9:49</td><td>Chang</td><td>No holding.</td><td>Easier: Just slow nose breathing</td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Two sniffs in, one long sigh out. No holding at any point. **Easier:** Just breathe slowly through your nose, making the out-breath a little longer. **Harder:** Build up to 5 minutes.

**Safety callouts:** If you feel light-headed, return to normal breathing.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 10:10–10:35 · Close

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>

</tbody></table>

## Script

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 0:00–0:35 · Welcome

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>0:00</td><td>Chang</td><td>Strong at 70. Pull and carry.</td><td>Strong at 70 · B1</td></tr>
<tr><td>0:10</td><td>Chang</td><td>Your back and your grip do the work you don't notice.</td><td>Stop if chest pain, dizziness or sharp pain</td></tr>
<tr><td>0:17</td><td>Chang</td><td>Bags, jugs, the band if you have it.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>0:24</td><td>Chang</td><td>Chest pain, dizziness or sharp pain: stop, sit, and call your doctor.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 0:35–1:00 · Ankle pumps

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>0:35</td><td>Chang</td><td>Sit tall. Chair against the wall.</td><td>Ankle pumps</td></tr>
<tr><td>0:42</td><td>Chang</td><td>Point your toes away, then pull them toward you. That's one pump.</td><td>Easier: Smaller movements</td></tr>
<tr><td>0:46</td><td>Chang</td><td>Big, slow movements.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>0:50</td><td>Chang</td><td>Feel your calves work.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>0:54</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe slowly.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Big, slow movements. Feel your calves work. **Easier:** Smaller movements. **Harder:** Lift one foot off the floor while you circle.

**Safety callouts:** Great before you stand up from sitting or lying. Sit a moment before you stand, then stand slowly while holding something steady.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 1:00–1:40 · March

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>1:00</td><td>Chang</td><td>Stand slowly. Hand on the counter.</td><td>March</td></tr>
<tr><td>1:19</td><td>Chang</td><td>March. Easy rhythm. Breathe steady.</td><td>Easier: Sit and march</td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Stand tall. Knee up, foot down softly. **Easier:** Sit and do the seated march. **Harder:** Lift knees higher, march faster, or let one hand hover above the counter.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 1:40–2:00 · Shoulder rolls

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>1:40</td><td>Chang</td><td>Sit tall. Chair against the wall.</td><td>Shoulder rolls</td></tr>
<tr><td>1:46</td><td>Chang</td><td>Lift your shoulders up toward your ears.</td><td>Easier: Just shrug and let go</td></tr>
<tr><td>1:49</td><td>Chang</td><td>Big, slow circles, backward.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>1:52</td><td>Chang</td><td>Let your arms hang heavy.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>1:55</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe in as you lift, out as you roll down.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Big, slow circles, backward. Let your arms hang heavy. **Easier:** Just shrug up and let go. **Harder:** Add arm circles: small circles out to the sides, forward and back.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 2:00–3:30 · Row

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>2:00</td><td>Chang</td><td>Hand on the counter. Chair behind you.</td><td>Row</td></tr>
<tr><td>2:17</td><td>Chang</td><td>Pull the jug up toward your ribs, elbow close to your body.</td><td>Easier: Towel pull or lighter jug</td></tr>
<tr><td>2:31</td><td>Chang</td><td>Pull with your elbow, not your hand.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>2:40</td><td>Chang</td><td>One... two... breathe out... three... slow down... four.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>2:46</td><td>Chang</td><td>Long back. Don't twist.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>3:00</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe out as you pull.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Pull with your elbow, not your hand. Long back. Don't twist. **Easier:** Stand upright and pull a towel looped around a sturdy door handle (see Towel row), or use a lighter jug. **Harder:** Full gallon jug (about 8 pounds), or a bag with a few cans. Pause for one second at the top.

**Safety callouts:** Osteoporosis: keep the hinge small and the back long. Check the band for nicks before every use. Door must open away from you and be locked.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 3:30–5:00 · Step-ups

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>3:30</td><td>Chang</td><td>Hand on the rail.</td><td>Step-ups</td></tr>
<tr><td>3:47</td><td>Chang</td><td>Step up with your right foot, placing the whole foot on the step.</td><td>Easier: Toe taps, hand on rail</td></tr>
<tr><td>4:01</td><td>Chang</td><td>Whole foot on the step, not just the toes.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>4:10</td><td>Chang</td><td>One... two... breathe out... three... slow down... four.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>4:16</td><td>Chang</td><td>Push through the heel of the top foot.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>4:30</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe out as you step up.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Whole foot on the step, not just the toes. Push through the heel of the top foot. Rail hand stays on the rail. **Easier:** Toe taps: tap the step with one foot, then the other, holding the rail. Or use a lower step, like a sturdy doorway threshold. **Harder:** Step up without pushing off the bottom foot. Later: carry a light bag of groceries in the hand that isn't on the rail.

**Safety callouts:** If stairs make you dizzy or you have fallen on stairs, do toe taps only until you've practiced balance for two weeks.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 5:00–6:20 · Hinge

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>5:00</td><td>Chang</td><td>Hand on the counter. Chair behind you.</td><td>Hinge</td></tr>
<tr><td>5:15</td><td>Chang</td><td>Push your hips back, like closing a car door with your bottom.</td><td>Easier: Smaller hinge, hands stay down</td></tr>
<tr><td>5:28</td><td>Chang</td><td>Hips go back, not down.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>5:36</td><td>Chang</td><td>One... two... breathe out... three... slow down... four.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>5:41</td><td>Chang</td><td>Long back, chest proud. No rounding.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>5:54</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe out as you stand tall.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Hips go back, not down. Long back, chest proud. No rounding. Stand up by squeezing your buttocks. **Easier:** Smaller movement, hands stay on the counter the whole time. **Harder:** Pick up a jug of water from the seat of a chair using the same hinge, and set it back down. Later: from a lower surface, like a step.

**Safety callouts:** Osteoporosis: this is the safe bending pattern. Keep the back long, never curl. Osteoporosis or a past spine fracture: this is the safe way to bend. Keep your back long; never round forward under load.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 6:20–7:15 · Curls

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>6:20</td><td>Chang</td><td>Sit tall. Chair against the wall.</td><td>Curls</td></tr>
<tr><td>6:31</td><td>Chang</td><td>Bend your elbows and bring the bottles toward your shoulders.</td><td>Easier: One arm, or empty bottles</td></tr>
<tr><td>6:40</td><td>Chang</td><td>Elbows stay by your sides.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>6:44</td><td>Chang</td><td>One... two... breathe out... three... slow down... four.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>6:49</td><td>Chang</td><td>No swinging.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>6:58</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe out as you curl up.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Elbows stay by your sides. No swinging. **Easier:** One arm at a time, or empty bottles. **Harder:** Heavier: a half-gallon jug (about 4 pounds), then a full gallon jug (about 8 pounds), one at a time.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 7:15–8:25 · One-side carry

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>7:15</td><td>Chang</td><td>Clear path. Free hand trails along the counter.</td><td>One-side carry</td></tr>
<tr><td>7:29</td><td>Chang</td><td>Stand tall. Don't lean away from the bag.</td><td>Easier: Lighter bag, hand on counter</td></tr>
<tr><td>7:40</td><td>Chang</td><td>Tall like a lamppost.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>7:51</td><td>Chang</td><td>Shoulders level.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>8:02</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe steadily. You should be able to talk.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Tall like a lamppost. Shoulders level. **Easier:** A lighter bag, free hand on the counter the whole time. **Harder:** A heavier bag, or a longer walk.

**Safety callouts:** Hand arthritis flaring today? Squeeze gently, or skip and do the finger spread only. Pick up and put down with a hinge. Never round your back to lift.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 8:25–9:05 · Towel wring

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>8:25</td><td>Chang</td><td>Sit tall. Chair against the wall.</td><td>Towel wring</td></tr>
<tr><td>8:34</td><td>Chang</td><td>Wring the towel hard, like squeezing out water: right hand one way, left hand the other.</td><td>Easier: Squeeze a rolled sock</td></tr>
<tr><td>8:40</td><td>Chang</td><td>Squeeze from your whole hand, not just your fingertips.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>8:47</td><td>Chang</td><td>Shoulders relaxed.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>8:53</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe out as you squeeze.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Squeeze from your whole hand, not just your fingertips. Shoulders relaxed. **Easier:** Squeeze a soft ball or rolled sock instead. **Harder:** Use a damp towel, or hold each wring for five seconds.

**Safety callouts:** Hand arthritis flaring today? Squeeze gently, or skip and do the finger spread only.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 9:05–9:45 · Calf stretch

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>9:05</td><td>Chang</td><td>Hand on the counter. Chair behind you.</td><td>Calf stretch</td></tr>
<tr><td>9:14</td><td>Chang</td><td>Bend the front knee and lean gently toward the wall until you feel a stretch in the back calf.</td><td>Easier: Smaller step back</td></tr>
<tr><td>9:20</td><td>Chang</td><td>Back heel stays down.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>9:27</td><td>Chang</td><td>Toes point forward.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>9:33</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe slowly through the stretch.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Back heel stays down. Toes point forward. **Easier:** Smaller step back. **Harder:** Bigger step back, or bend the back knee slightly to reach the lower calf.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 9:45–10:25 · Cyclic sighing

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>9:45</td><td>Chang</td><td>Sit. Two sniffs in through the nose. One long sigh out.</td><td>Cyclic sighing</td></tr>
<tr><td>10:04</td><td>Chang</td><td>No holding.</td><td>Easier: Just slow nose breathing</td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Two sniffs in, one long sigh out. No holding at any point. **Easier:** Just breathe slowly through your nose, making the out-breath a little longer. **Harder:** Build up to 5 minutes.

**Safety callouts:** If you feel light-headed, return to normal breathing.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 10:25–10:50 · Close

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>10:25</td><td>Chang</td><td>Pull and carry. That's groceries, grandkids and doors.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>10:38</td><td>Chang</td><td>Monday: legs again.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

</div>


# S70-A2 · Phase 2 (Build): Power and floor

| Type | Length | Set | Wardrobe | Voices |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Strong at 70 program | 10:30 | SET-GARAGE | C-TRAIN-A | Chang |

<div class="box stop" markdown="1">
<span class="label">On screen the whole session:</span> the "AI character" corner tag. In the first 30 seconds and before each hard block: "Stop if chest pain, dizziness or sharp pain."
</div>

<div class="box note" markdown="1">
<span class="label">Gentle-day swaps (the sore knee / sore back / low energy button):</span> **Sore knee:** Use the Rebuild version of any standing leg move; skip floor practice and stairs today. **Sore back:** Seated versions of hinges and carries; keep every bend long-backed. **Low energy:** Do the warm-up, the first two blocks and the cool-down.
</div>

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>2:00</td><td>Chang</td><td>Hand on the counter. Chair behind you.</td><td>Power stands</td></tr>
<tr><td>2:19</td><td>Chang</td><td>Sit tall, feet flat, arms crossed or hands on thighs.</td><td>Easier: Normal speed, hands on thighs</td></tr>
<tr><td>2:35</td><td>Chang</td><td>Fast up, slow down.</td><td>Advanced (Iron): not your starting point</td></tr>
<tr><td>2:45</td><td>Chang</td><td>One... two... breathe out... three... slow down... four.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>2:51</td><td>Chang</td><td>Quick is not the same as sloppy. Knees stay over toes.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>3:07</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe out hard as you stand.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Fast up, slow down. Quick is not the same as sloppy. Knees stay over toes. **Easier:** Normal-speed sit-to-stand with hands on your thighs. **Harder:** Hold a jug of water at your chest, or pause one second just above the seat on the way down.

**Safety callouts:** Stop the fast part if you feel dizzy when you stand. Go back to normal speed.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 3:40–5:05 · Push

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>3:40</td><td>Chang</td><td>Hand on the counter. Chair behind you.</td><td>Push</td></tr>
<tr><td>3:56</td><td>Chang</td><td>Lower your chest toward the counter edge.</td><td>Easier: Wall push-ups</td></tr>
<tr><td>4:10</td><td>Chang</td><td>Straight line from head to heels.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>4:18</td><td>Chang</td><td>One... two... breathe out... three... slow down... four.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>4:23</td><td>Chang</td><td>Squeeze your buttocks so your hips don't sag.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>4:37</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe out as you push up.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Straight line from head to heels. Squeeze your buttocks so your hips don't sag. **Easier:** Wall push-ups. **Harder:** Lower slowly for three seconds. Later (Iron track): a sturdy low bench or bottom stair, only if the counter version is easy for 12 reps.

**Safety callouts:** Wrist pain? Make fists or hold the counter edge instead of flat palms.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 5:05–6:35 · Floor practice

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>5:05</td><td>Chang</td><td>Chair beside you. Towel down. Someone else home.</td><td>Floor practice</td></tr>
<tr><td>5:32</td><td>Chang</td><td>Kneel. Then front foot flat. Push up with hands on the chair.</td><td>Easier: Half-kneel only, or chair stands</td></tr>
<tr><td>5:56</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe out as you rise. Earn the floor.</td><td>Only with a sturdy chair and someone home</td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Hands on the chair the whole time. Slow down. Up is a push, not a jump. **Easier:** Only the first step: lower into a half-kneel on the towel and come back up, holding the chair. Or skip the floor and do sit-to-stands. **Harder:** Iron: from kneeling, sit down onto the floor beside the chair, then roll to your knees and rise with the chair. Only with someone home.

**Safety callouts:** Only try the floor with a sturdy chair or sofa next to you and someone home. Recent hip or knee replacement, or severe knee arthritis: follow your surgeon's or physical therapist's guidance first. New knee? Kneeling may not be allowed yet. Ask your surgeon. Sit a moment before you stand, then stand slowly while holding something steady.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 6:35–7:50 · Suitcase lift

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>6:35</td><td>Chang</td><td>Hand on the counter. Chair behind you.</td><td>Suitcase lift</td></tr>
<tr><td>6:50</td><td>Chang</td><td>Push your hips back with a long back and bend your knees a little.</td><td>Easier: Lighter jug, higher surface</td></tr>
<tr><td>7:02</td><td>Chang</td><td>Hips back. Long back.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>7:08</td><td>Chang</td><td>One... two... breathe out... three... slow down... four.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>7:14</td><td>Chang</td><td>Don't lean toward the jug. Stay square.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>7:26</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe out as you stand.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Hips back. Long back. Don't lean toward the jug. Stay square. **Easier:** A lighter jug, and lift it from a higher surface like the counter's edge of a table. **Harder:** A heavier bag, or lift from the bottom step instead of the chair.

**Safety callouts:** Osteoporosis: this is the safe bending pattern. Keep the back long, never curl. Osteoporosis or a past spine fracture: long back always, never round to reach.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 7:50–8:45 · High wall sit

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>7:50</td><td>Chang</td><td>Back on the wall. A few inches down. Chair beside you.</td><td>High wall sit</td></tr>
<tr><td>8:07</td><td>Chang</td><td>Keep talking. Count out loud.</td><td>Easier: Only 2 inches down, 10 s</td></tr>
<tr><td>8:22</td><td>Chang</td><td>High blood pressure? Short holds, and ask your doctor about longer ones.</td><td>Keep breathing: count out loud</td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Shallow is fine. This is not a contest of depth. Knees stay behind or over your toes. **Easier:** Slide down only 2 inches, or hold for just 10 seconds. **Harder:** Slide a little lower (never below where your knees are bent to a right angle), or hold up to 30 seconds.

**Safety callouts:** Breathe through it. High blood pressure or a heart condition? Ask your doctor before long holds.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 8:45–9:25 · Calf stretch

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>8:45</td><td>Chang</td><td>Hand on the counter. Chair behind you.</td><td>Calf stretch</td></tr>
<tr><td>8:54</td><td>Chang</td><td>Bend the front knee and lean gently toward the wall until you feel a stretch in the back calf.</td><td>Easier: Smaller step back</td></tr>
<tr><td>9:00</td><td>Chang</td><td>Back heel stays down.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>9:07</td><td>Chang</td><td>Toes point forward.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>9:13</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe slowly through the stretch.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Back heel stays down. Toes point forward. **Easier:** Smaller step back. **Harder:** Bigger step back, or bend the back knee slightly to reach the lower calf.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 9:25–10:05 · Cyclic sighing

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>9:25</td><td>Chang</td><td>Sit. Two sniffs in through the nose. One long sigh out.</td><td>Cyclic sighing</td></tr>
<tr><td>9:44</td><td>Chang</td><td>No holding.</td><td>Easier: Just slow nose breathing</td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Two sniffs in, one long sigh out. No holding at any point. **Easier:** Just breathe slowly through your nose, making the out-breath a little longer. **Harder:** Build up to 5 minutes.

**Safety callouts:** If you feel light-headed, return to normal breathing.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 10:05–10:30 · Close

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>10:05</td><td>Chang</td><td>Getting up fast is what saves you when you trip.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>10:18</td><td>Chang</td><td>Thursday: stairs and carries.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

</div>


# S70-B2 · Phase 2 (Build): Stairs and carries

| Type | Length | Set | Wardrobe | Voices |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Strong at 70 program | 10:25 | SET-STOOP | C-TRAIN-A | Chang |

<div class="box stop" markdown="1">
<span class="label">On screen the whole session:</span> the "AI character" corner tag. In the first 30 seconds and before each hard block: "Stop if chest pain, dizziness or sharp pain."
</div>

<div class="box note" markdown="1">
<span class="label">Gentle-day swaps (the sore knee / sore back / low energy button):</span> **Sore knee:** Use the Rebuild version of any standing leg move; skip floor practice and stairs today. **Sore back:** Seated versions of hinges and carries; keep every bend long-backed. **Low energy:** Do the warm-up, the first two blocks and the cool-down.
</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 0:35–1:00 · Ankle pumps

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>0:35</td><td>Chang</td><td>Sit tall. Chair against the wall.</td><td>Ankle pumps</td></tr>
<tr><td>0:42</td><td>Chang</td><td>Point your toes away, then pull them toward you. That's one pump.</td><td>Easier: Smaller movements</td></tr>
<tr><td>0:46</td><td>Chang</td><td>Big, slow movements.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>0:50</td><td>Chang</td><td>Feel your calves work.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>0:54</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe slowly.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Big, slow movements. Feel your calves work. **Easier:** Smaller movements. **Harder:** Lift one foot off the floor while you circle.

**Safety callouts:** Great before you stand up from sitting or lying. Sit a moment before you stand, then stand slowly while holding something steady.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 1:00–1:40 · March

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>1:00</td><td>Chang</td><td>Stand slowly. Hand on the counter.</td><td>March</td></tr>
<tr><td>1:19</td><td>Chang</td><td>March. Easy rhythm. Breathe steady.</td><td>Easier: Sit and march</td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Stand tall. Knee up, foot down softly. **Easier:** Sit and do the seated march. **Harder:** Lift knees higher, march faster, or let one hand hover above the counter.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 1:40–2:00 · Shoulder rolls

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>1:40</td><td>Chang</td><td>Sit tall. Chair against the wall.</td><td>Shoulder rolls</td></tr>
<tr><td>1:46</td><td>Chang</td><td>Lift your shoulders up toward your ears.</td><td>Easier: Just shrug and let go</td></tr>
<tr><td>1:49</td><td>Chang</td><td>Big, slow circles, backward.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>1:52</td><td>Chang</td><td>Let your arms hang heavy.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>1:55</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe in as you lift, out as you roll down.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Big, slow circles, backward. Let your arms hang heavy. **Easier:** Just shrug up and let go. **Harder:** Add arm circles: small circles out to the sides, forward and back.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 2:00–3:40 · Stair practice

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>2:00</td><td>Chang</td><td>Hand on the rail.</td><td>Stair practice</td></tr>
<tr><td>2:19</td><td>Chang</td><td>Walk up one step at a time at a steady pace, whole foot on each step.</td><td>Easier: Bottom 3 steps only</td></tr>
<tr><td>2:35</td><td>Chang</td><td>Whole foot on the step.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>2:51</td><td>Chang</td><td>Rail hand never lets go.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>3:07</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe steadily. Rest at the top as long as you like.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Whole foot on the step. Rail hand never lets go. **Easier:** Just the bottom 3 steps, up and down. **Harder:** Two flights, or carry a light bag in the free hand.

**Safety callouts:** Chest pain or unusual breathlessness on stairs: stop, sit, and call your doctor.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 3:40–5:00 · Row

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>3:40</td><td>Chang</td><td>Sit or stand with the chair behind you. Check the band first.</td><td>Row</td></tr>
<tr><td>3:55</td><td>Chang</td><td>Pull your elbows back past your ribs.</td><td>Easier: Closer to the door, or towel</td></tr>
<tr><td>4:08</td><td>Chang</td><td>Elbows close to your body.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>4:16</td><td>Chang</td><td>One... two... breathe out... three... slow down... four.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>4:21</td><td>Chang</td><td>Tall chest, shoulders down.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>4:34</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe out as you pull.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Elbows close to your body. Tall chest, shoulders down. **Easier:** Sit closer to the door so the band is slacker, or do the towel pull-apart. **Harder:** Scoot back for more tension, or pause 2 seconds with elbows back.

**Safety callouts:** Check the band for nicks before every use. Door must open away from you and be locked.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 5:00–6:10 · Two-hand carry

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>5:00</td><td>Chang</td><td>Clear path. Walk along the counter or a hallway wall.</td><td>Two-hand carry</td></tr>
<tr><td>5:14</td><td>Chang</td><td>Stand tall, shoulders down.</td><td>Easier: One light bag, hand on counter</td></tr>
<tr><td>5:25</td><td>Chang</td><td>Tall, like you're proud of the groceries.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>5:36</td><td>Chang</td><td>Short, steady steps.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>5:47</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe steadily. You should be able to talk.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Tall, like you're proud of the groceries. Short, steady steps. **Easier:** One light bag, and keep your free hand trailing along the counter. **Harder:** Heavier: two full gallon jugs (about 8 pounds each). Iron track: two heavier bags or kettlebells.

**Safety callouts:** Hand arthritis flaring today? Squeeze gently, or skip and do the finger spread only. Pick up and put down with a hinge. Never round your back to lift.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 6:10–7:00 · Band pull-apart

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>6:10</td><td>Chang</td><td>Sit or stand with the chair behind you. Check the band first.</td><td>Band pull-apart</td></tr>
<tr><td>6:21</td><td>Chang</td><td>Pull the band apart toward your chest by opening your arms.</td><td>Easier: Hands wider on the band</td></tr>
<tr><td>6:29</td><td>Chang</td><td>Shoulders down.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>6:32</td><td>Chang</td><td>One... two... breathe out... three... slow down... four.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>6:37</td><td>Chang</td><td>Slow on the way back.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>6:45</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe out as you pull apart.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Shoulders down. Slow on the way back. **Easier:** Hands wider apart on the band (less tension), or the towel pull-apart. **Harder:** Hands closer together, or a 2-second squeeze.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 7:00–8:00 · Overhead press

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>7:00</td><td>Chang</td><td>Sit tall. Chair against the wall.</td><td>Overhead press</td></tr>
<tr><td>7:12</td><td>Chang</td><td>Press the bottles up toward the ceiling, only as high as is comfortable.</td><td>Easier: One arm, press at a slant</td></tr>
<tr><td>7:22</td><td>Chang</td><td>Ribs down. Don't arch your back.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>7:27</td><td>Chang</td><td>One... two... breathe out... three... slow down... four.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>7:31</td><td>Chang</td><td>Only to comfortable height.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>7:41</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe out as you press up.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Ribs down. Don't arch your back. Only to comfortable height. **Easier:** One arm at a time, or press forward and up at a slant instead of straight up. **Harder:** Heavier bottles or a half-gallon jug in each hand; stand at the counter to press.

**Safety callouts:** Shoulder pain or a known rotator cuff problem? Only lift to a comfortable height, or skip it.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 8:00–8:40 · Towel wring

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>8:00</td><td>Chang</td><td>Sit tall. Chair against the wall.</td><td>Towel wring</td></tr>
<tr><td>8:09</td><td>Chang</td><td>Wring the towel hard, like squeezing out water: right hand one way, left hand the other.</td><td>Easier: Squeeze a rolled sock</td></tr>
<tr><td>8:15</td><td>Chang</td><td>Squeeze from your whole hand, not just your fingertips.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>8:22</td><td>Chang</td><td>Shoulders relaxed.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>8:28</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe out as you squeeze.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Squeeze from your whole hand, not just your fingertips. Shoulders relaxed. **Easier:** Squeeze a soft ball or rolled sock instead. **Harder:** Use a damp towel, or hold each wring for five seconds.

**Safety callouts:** Hand arthritis flaring today? Squeeze gently, or skip and do the finger spread only.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 8:40–9:20 · Calf stretch

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>8:40</td><td>Chang</td><td>Hand on the counter. Chair behind you.</td><td>Calf stretch</td></tr>
<tr><td>8:49</td><td>Chang</td><td>Bend the front knee and lean gently toward the wall until you feel a stretch in the back calf.</td><td>Easier: Smaller step back</td></tr>
<tr><td>8:55</td><td>Chang</td><td>Back heel stays down.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>9:02</td><td>Chang</td><td>Toes point forward.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>9:08</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe slowly through the stretch.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Back heel stays down. Toes point forward. **Easier:** Smaller step back. **Harder:** Bigger step back, or bend the back knee slightly to reach the lower calf.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 9:20–10:00 · Cyclic sighing

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>9:20</td><td>Chang</td><td>Sit. Two sniffs in through the nose. One long sigh out.</td><td>Cyclic sighing</td></tr>
<tr><td>9:39</td><td>Chang</td><td>No holding.</td><td>Easier: Just slow nose breathing</td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Two sniffs in, one long sigh out. No holding at any point. **Easier:** Just breathe slowly through your nose, making the out-breath a little longer. **Harder:** Build up to 5 minutes.

**Safety callouts:** If you feel light-headed, return to normal breathing.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 10:00–10:25 · Close

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>

<tr><td>10:13</td><td>Chang</td><td>Rest well.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

</div>

## Script

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 0:00–0:35 · Welcome

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>0:00</td><td>Chang</td><td>Phase three. Strong.</td><td>Strong at 70 · A3</td></tr>
<tr><td>0:10</td><td>Chang</td><td>Heavier where you can, slower where you can't.</td><td>Stop if chest pain, dizziness or sharp pain</td></tr>
<tr><td>0:17</td><td>Chang</td><td>Chair against the wall. Someone home for the floor.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>0:24</td><td>Chang</td><td>Chest pain, dizziness or sharp pain: stop, sit, and call your doctor.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 0:35–1:00 · Ankle pumps

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>0:35</td><td>Chang</td><td>Sit tall. Chair against the wall.</td><td>Ankle pumps</td></tr>
<tr><td>0:42</td><td>Chang</td><td>Point your toes away, then pull them toward you. That's one pump.</td><td>Easier: Smaller movements</td></tr>
<tr><td>0:46</td><td>Chang</td><td>Big, slow movements.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>0:50</td><td>Chang</td><td>Feel your calves work.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>0:54</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe slowly.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Big, slow movements. Feel your calves work. **Easier:** Smaller movements. **Harder:** Lift one foot off the floor while you circle.

**Safety callouts:** Great before you stand up from sitting or lying. Sit a moment before you stand, then stand slowly while holding something steady.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 1:00–1:40 · March

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>1:00</td><td>Chang</td><td>Stand slowly. Hand on the counter.</td><td>March</td></tr>
<tr><td>1:19</td><td>Chang</td><td>March. Easy rhythm. Breathe steady.</td><td>Easier: Sit and march</td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Stand tall. Knee up, foot down softly. **Easier:** Sit and do the seated march. **Harder:** Lift knees higher, march faster, or let one hand hover above the counter.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 1:40–2:00 · Shoulder rolls

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>1:40</td><td>Chang</td><td>Sit tall. Chair against the wall.</td><td>Shoulder rolls</td></tr>
<tr><td>1:46</td><td>Chang</td><td>Lift your shoulders up toward your ears.</td><td>Easier: Just shrug and let go</td></tr>
<tr><td>1:49</td><td>Chang</td><td>Big, slow circles, backward.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>1:52</td><td>Chang</td><td>Let your arms hang heavy.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>1:55</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe in as you lift, out as you roll down.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Big, slow circles, backward. Let your arms hang heavy. **Easier:** Just shrug up and let go. **Harder:** Add arm circles: small circles out to the sides, forward and back.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 2:00–3:50 · Legs

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>2:00</td><td>Chang</td><td>Hand on the counter. Chair behind you.</td><td>Legs</td></tr>
<tr><td>2:20</td><td>Chang</td><td>Cross your arms over your chest, or rest your hands on your thighs.</td><td>Easier: Higher seat, hands on thighs</td></tr>
<tr><td>2:38</td><td>Chang</td><td>Nose over toes.</td><td>Advanced (Iron): not your starting point</td></tr>
<tr><td>2:49</td><td>Chang</td><td>One... two... breathe out... three... slow down... four.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>2:55</td><td>Chang</td><td>Knees point the same way as your toes. Don't let them cave inward.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>3:13</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe out as you stand. Breathe in as you sit.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Nose over toes. Knees point the same way as your toes. Don't let them cave inward. Sit down slow. Two or three seconds. **Easier:** Put a firm cushion or folded blanket on the seat to make it higher, or push up with your hands on your thighs or on chair arms. **Harder:** Arms crossed, lower for a slow count of three, and pause one second just above the seat before touching down. Later: hold a gallon jug of water at your chest.

**Safety callouts:** Advanced. Only if your knees feel good with step-ups.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 3:50–5:10 · Push

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>3:50</td><td>Chang</td><td>Hand on the counter. Chair behind you.</td><td>Push</td></tr>
<tr><td>4:05</td><td>Chang</td><td>Lower your chest toward the counter edge.</td><td>Easier: Wall push-ups</td></tr>
<tr><td>4:18</td><td>Chang</td><td>Straight line from head to heels.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>4:26</td><td>Chang</td><td>One... two... breathe out... three... slow down... four.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>4:31</td><td>Chang</td><td>Squeeze your buttocks so your hips don't sag.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>4:44</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe out as you push up.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Straight line from head to heels. Squeeze your buttocks so your hips don't sag. **Easier:** Wall push-ups. **Harder:** Lower slowly for three seconds. Later (Iron track): a sturdy low bench or bottom stair, only if the counter version is easy for 12 reps.

**Safety callouts:** Wrist pain? Make fists or hold the counter edge instead of flat palms.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 5:10–6:40 · Floor practice

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>5:10</td><td>Chang</td><td>Chair beside you. Towel down. Someone home.</td><td>Floor practice</td></tr>
<tr><td>5:37</td><td>Chang</td><td>Down with control. Up with a push. Breathe out.</td><td>Easier: Half-kneel only, or chair stands</td></tr>
<tr><td>6:01</td><td>Chang</td><td>Stand still a moment before you walk.</td><td>Only with a sturdy chair and someone home</td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Hands on the chair the whole time. Slow down. Up is a push, not a jump. **Easier:** Only the first step: lower into a half-kneel on the towel and come back up, holding the chair. Or skip the floor and do sit-to-stands. **Harder:** Iron: from kneeling, sit down onto the floor beside the chair, then roll to your knees and rise with the chair. Only with someone home.

**Safety callouts:** Only try the floor with a sturdy chair or sofa next to you and someone home. Recent hip or knee replacement, or severe knee arthritis: follow your surgeon's or physical therapist's guidance first. New knee? Kneeling may not be allowed yet. Ask your surgeon. Sit a moment before you stand, then stand slowly while holding something steady.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 6:40–7:55 · Suitcase lift

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>6:40</td><td>Chang</td><td>Hand on the counter. Chair behind you.</td><td>Suitcase lift</td></tr>
<tr><td>6:55</td><td>Chang</td><td>Push your hips back with a long back and bend your knees a little.</td><td>Easier: Lighter jug, higher surface</td></tr>
<tr><td>7:07</td><td>Chang</td><td>Hips back. Long back.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>7:13</td><td>Chang</td><td>One... two... breathe out... three... slow down... four.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>7:19</td><td>Chang</td><td>Don't lean toward the jug. Stay square.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>7:31</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe out as you stand.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Hips back. Long back. Don't lean toward the jug. Stay square. **Easier:** A lighter jug, and lift it from a higher surface like the counter's edge of a table. **Harder:** A heavier bag, or lift from the bottom step instead of the chair.

**Safety callouts:** Osteoporosis: this is the safe bending pattern. Keep the back long, never curl. Osteoporosis or a past spine fracture: long back always, never round to reach.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 7:55–8:45 · Heel raises

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>7:55</td><td>Chang</td><td>Hand on the counter. Chair behind you.</td><td>Heel raises</td></tr>
<tr><td>8:06</td><td>Chang</td><td>Rise up onto the balls of your feet, as high as is comfortable.</td><td>Easier: Seated, or rise halfway</td></tr>
<tr><td>8:14</td><td>Chang</td><td>Tall like someone is pulling a string on top of your head.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>8:17</td><td>Chang</td><td>One... two... breathe out... three... slow down... four.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>8:22</td><td>Chang</td><td>Weight over the big toe and second toe, not rolling out.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>8:30</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe out as you rise.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Tall like someone is pulling a string on top of your head. Weight over the big toe and second toe, not rolling out. **Easier:** Sit in your chair and raise your heels from there, or hold the counter with both hands and rise only halfway. **Harder:** One hand on the counter. Later: one leg at a time, with both hands on the counter.

**Safety callouts:** Calf cramps are common at first. Stretch and walk them out. One calf that is swollen, red and painful is not a cramp: that is for your doctor, today.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 8:45–9:25 · Calf stretch

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>8:45</td><td>Chang</td><td>Hand on the counter. Chair behind you.</td><td>Calf stretch</td></tr>
<tr><td>8:54</td><td>Chang</td><td>Bend the front knee and lean gently toward the wall until you feel a stretch in the back calf.</td><td>Easier: Smaller step back</td></tr>
<tr><td>9:00</td><td>Chang</td><td>Back heel stays down.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>9:07</td><td>Chang</td><td>Toes point forward.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>9:13</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe slowly through the stretch.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Back heel stays down. Toes point forward. **Easier:** Smaller step back. **Harder:** Bigger step back, or bend the back knee slightly to reach the lower calf.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 9:25–10:05 · Cyclic sighing

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>9:25</td><td>Chang</td><td>Sit. Two sniffs in through the nose. One long sigh out.</td><td>Cyclic sighing</td></tr>
<tr><td>9:44</td><td>Chang</td><td>No holding.</td><td>Easier: Just slow nose breathing</td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Two sniffs in, one long sigh out. No holding at any point. **Easier:** Just breathe slowly through your nose, making the out-breath a little longer. **Harder:** Build up to 5 minutes.

**Safety callouts:** If you feel light-headed, return to normal breathing.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 10:05–10:30 · Close

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>10:05</td><td>Chang</td><td>Twelve weeks ago, this was a lot. Look at you.</td><td></td></tr>

</tbody></table>

<tr><td>1:49</td><td>Chang</td><td>Big, slow circles, backward.</td><td></td></tr>

<tr><td>1:55</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe in as you lift, out as you roll down.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Big, slow circles, backward. Let your arms hang heavy. **Easier:** Just shrug up and let go. **Harder:** Add arm circles: small circles out to the sides, forward and back.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 2:00–3:35 · Step-ups

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>2:00</td><td>Chang</td><td>Hand on the rail.</td><td>Step-ups</td></tr>
<tr><td>2:18</td><td>Chang</td><td>Step up with your right foot, placing the whole foot on the step.</td><td>Easier: Toe taps, hand on rail</td></tr>
<tr><td>2:33</td><td>Chang</td><td>Whole foot on the step, not just the toes.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>2:42</td><td>Chang</td><td>One... two... breathe out... three... slow down... four.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>2:48</td><td>Chang</td><td>Push through the heel of the top foot.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>3:03</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe out as you step up.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Whole foot on the step, not just the toes. Push through the heel of the top foot. Rail hand stays on the rail. **Easier:** Toe taps: tap the step with one foot, then the other, holding the rail. Or use a lower step, like a sturdy doorway threshold. **Harder:** Step up without pushing off the bottom foot. Later: carry a light bag of groceries in the hand that isn't on the rail.

**Safety callouts:** If stairs make you dizzy or you have fallen on stairs, do toe taps only until you've practiced balance for two weeks.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 3:35–4:55 · Row

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>3:35</td><td>Chang</td><td>Sit or stand with the chair behind you. Check the band first.</td><td>Row</td></tr>
<tr><td>3:50</td><td>Chang</td><td>Pull your elbows back past your ribs.</td><td>Easier: Closer to the door, or towel</td></tr>
<tr><td>4:03</td><td>Chang</td><td>Elbows close to your body.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>4:11</td><td>Chang</td><td>One... two... breathe out... three... slow down... four.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>4:16</td><td>Chang</td><td>Tall chest, shoulders down.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>4:29</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe out as you pull.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Elbows close to your body. Tall chest, shoulders down. **Easier:** Sit closer to the door so the band is slacker, or do the towel pull-apart. **Harder:** Scoot back for more tension, or pause 2 seconds with elbows back.

**Safety callouts:** Check the band for nicks before every use. Door must open away from you and be locked. Osteoporosis: keep the hinge small and the back long.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 4:55–5:55 · Band press-out

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>4:55</td><td>Chang</td><td>Sit or stand with the chair behind you. Check the band first.</td><td>Band press-out</td></tr>
<tr><td>5:07</td><td>Chang</td><td>Press your hands straight out in front of your chest.</td><td>Easier: Seated, closer to the door</td></tr>
<tr><td>5:17</td><td>Chang</td><td>Stay square. The band pulls, you don't turn.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>5:22</td><td>Chang</td><td>One... two... breathe out... three... slow down... four.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>5:26</td><td>Chang</td><td>Ribs down.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>5:36</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe out as you press.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Stay square. The band pulls, you don't turn. Ribs down. **Easier:** Do it seated, or stand closer to the door. **Harder:** Step farther from the door, or hold 5 seconds.

**Safety callouts:** Door must open away from you and be locked.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 5:55–7:10 · Two-hand carry

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>5:55</td><td>Chang</td><td>Clear path. Walk along the counter or a hallway wall.</td><td>Two-hand carry</td></tr>
<tr><td>6:10</td><td>Chang</td><td>Stand tall, shoulders down.</td><td>Easier: One light bag, hand on counter</td></tr>
<tr><td>6:22</td><td>Chang</td><td>Tall, like you're proud of the groceries.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>6:34</td><td>Chang</td><td>Short, steady steps.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>6:46</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe steadily. You should be able to talk.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Tall, like you're proud of the groceries. Short, steady steps. **Easier:** One light bag, and keep your free hand trailing along the counter. **Harder:** Heavier: two full gallon jugs (about 8 pounds each). Iron track: two heavier bags or kettlebells.

**Safety callouts:** Hand arthritis flaring today? Squeeze gently, or skip and do the finger spread only. Pick up and put down with a hinge. Never round your back to lift.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 7:10–8:05 · Curls

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>7:10</td><td>Chang</td><td>Sit tall. Chair against the wall.</td><td>Curls</td></tr>
<tr><td>7:21</td><td>Chang</td><td>Bend your elbows and bring the bottles toward your shoulders.</td><td>Easier: One arm, or empty bottles</td></tr>
<tr><td>7:30</td><td>Chang</td><td>Elbows stay by your sides.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>7:34</td><td>Chang</td><td>One... two... breathe out... three... slow down... four.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>7:39</td><td>Chang</td><td>No swinging.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>7:48</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe out as you curl up.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Elbows stay by your sides. No swinging. **Easier:** One arm at a time, or empty bottles. **Harder:** Heavier: a half-gallon jug (about 4 pounds), then a full gallon jug (about 8 pounds), one at a time.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 8:05–8:45 · Calf stretch

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>8:05</td><td>Chang</td><td>Hand on the counter. Chair behind you.</td><td>Calf stretch</td></tr>
<tr><td>8:14</td><td>Chang</td><td>Bend the front knee and lean gently toward the wall until you feel a stretch in the back calf.</td><td>Easier: Smaller step back</td></tr>
<tr><td>8:20</td><td>Chang</td><td>Back heel stays down.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>8:27</td><td>Chang</td><td>Toes point forward.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>8:33</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe slowly through the stretch.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Back heel stays down. Toes point forward. **Easier:** Smaller step back. **Harder:** Bigger step back, or bend the back knee slightly to reach the lower calf.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 8:45–9:25 · Cyclic sighing

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>8:45</td><td>Chang</td><td>Sit. Two sniffs in through the nose. One long sigh out.</td><td>Cyclic sighing</td></tr>
<tr><td>9:04</td><td>Chang</td><td>No holding.</td><td>Easier: Just slow nose breathing</td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Two sniffs in, one long sigh out. No holding at any point. **Easier:** Just breathe slowly through your nose, making the out-breath a little longer. **Harder:** Build up to 5 minutes.

**Safety callouts:** If you feel light-headed, return to normal breathing.

</div>

# Where the numbers come from

Every number and health statement in this book traces to one of the entries below. They are the same evidence IDs our whole team uses (EVIDENCE.md). Grade A means a Cochrane review, a large meta-analysis or a guideline body. B means a single good trial or a small meta-analysis. C means an observational study: it shows a link, not cause and effect. D means lab, physiology or label data.


<div class="keep" markdown="1">

**E01** (grade A). Progressive resistance training in older adults: 121 RCTs, 6,700 people, 2–3×/week. Large effect on strength (SMD 0.84), moderate-to-large effect on getting out of a chair (SMD −0.94), gait speed +0.08 m/s, less osteoarthritis pain. Most side effects were minor soreness or joint pain.

<p class="src">Source: Liu & Latham, Cochrane 2009 — https://www.cochrane.org/evidence/CD002759_progressive-resistance-strength-training-improving-physical-function-older-adults</p>

</div>

<div class="keep" markdown="1">

**E02** (grade A). NSCA position statement: resistance training is safe and effective for older adults, including frail people. Progress gradually. Train 2–3×/week, 1–3 sets of 6–12 reps at 70–85% 1RM once adapted. Include power (fast lifting intent) and balance.

<p class="src">Source: Fragala et al., J Strength Cond Res 2019 — https://journals.lww.com/nsca-jscr/fulltext/2019/08000/resistance_training_for_older_adults__position.1.aspx</p>

</div>

<div class="keep" markdown="1">

**E03** (grade B (small)). Ten frail nursing-home residents aged ~90, 8 weeks of high-intensity leg training: strength +174%, thigh muscle area up about 9%, walking speed improved. Muscle still adapts in the 90s.

<p class="src">Source: Fiatarone et al., JAMA 1990 — https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/2342214/</p>

</div>

<div class="keep" markdown="1">

**E04** (grade A (review)). Around age 75, muscle mass drops about 0.6–1% per year while strength drops 2.5–4% per year. Strength declines 2–5× faster than mass.

<p class="src">Source: Mitchell et al., Frontiers in Physiology 2012 — https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/physiology/articles/10.3389/fphys.2012.00260/full</p>

</div>

<div class="keep" markdown="1">

**E06** (grade A (consensus)). Sarcopenia screening cut-offs (EWGSOP2): grip under 27 kg for men or under 16 kg for women, or 5 chair rises taking more than 15 s, signals "probable sarcopenia".

<p class="src">Source: Cruz-Jentoft et al., Age Ageing 2019 — https://www.esceo.org/sites/esceo/files/pdf/2019%20Age%20Ageing%20EWGSOP2.pdf</p>

</div>

<div class="keep" markdown="1">

**E08** (grade C). Sitting-rising test (sit to the floor and stand up without support; score 0–10, lose 1 point per hand/knee support). 2,002 adults aged 51–80. The lowest scorers (0–2) had 5–6× the death risk of the highest (8–10). Each +1 point was linked with 21% lower mortality.

<p class="src">Source: Brito, Araújo et al., Eur J Prev Cardiol 2012/2014 — https://www.sciencedaily.com/releases/2012/12/121213085202.htm</p>

</div>

<div class="keep" markdown="1">

**E11** (grade A (tool)). CDC STEADI 30-second chair stand (17-inch chair, arms crossed), used in the CDC's older-adult screening. Below-average scores: men 60–64 <14, 65–69 <12, 70–74 <12, 75–79 <11, 80–84 <10, 85–89 <8, 90–94 <7. Women 60–64 <12, 65–69 <11, 70–74 <10, 75–79 <10, 80–84 <9, 85–89 <8, 90–94 <4. If arms are used to stand, the score is 0.

<p class="src">Source: CDC STEADI — https://www.cdc.gov/steadi/media/pdfs/STEADI-Assessment-30Sec-508.pdf</p>

</div>

<div class="keep" markdown="1">

**E39** (grade A−). High-velocity "power" training (lift with fast intent, lower slowly) gives functional gains similar to or slightly better than traditional training in older adults, and it is safe when supervised and progressed.

<p class="src">Source: J Physiotherapy 2023 systematic review — https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S183695532300053X ; Eur Rev Aging Phys Act 2022 — https://link.springer.com/article/10.1186/s11556-022-00297-x</p>

</div>

<div class="keep" markdown="1">

**E40** (grade A (consensus)). Osteoporosis exercise guidance: do resistance and balance training. Avoid rapid, repeated or loaded spinal flexion (sit-ups, toe-touches with weight) and forceful twisting. Flexion-exercise programs were linked with more vertebral fractures.

<p class="src">Source: Giangregorio et al., "Too Fit To Fracture", Osteoporos Int 2014 — https://link.springer.com/10.1007/s00198-014-2881-4 ; Sinaki & Mikkelsen, Arch Phys Med Rehabil 1984</p>

</div>

<div class="keep" markdown="1">

**E41** (grade B (known literature)). Pain-monitoring model: during and after exercise, pain up to about 3/10 (we use a conservative threshold) is acceptable if it settles by the next morning and isn't trending up week to week.

<p class="src">Source: Thomeé, Phys Ther 1997; Silbernagel et al., Am J Sports Med 2007</p>

</div>

<div class="keep" markdown="1">

**E42** (grade A (statement)). AHA scientific statement (2023): resistance training is recommended for adults with and without cardiovascular disease. It lowers blood pressure and improves glucose control and function. Avoid breath-holding (Valsalva). People with CVD should get individualized clearance.

<p class="src">Source: Paluch et al., Circulation 2024 — https://www.ahajournals.org/doi/10.1161/CIR.0000000000001189</p>

</div>

<div class="keep" markdown="1">

**E43** (grade A (guideline)). Pre-exercise screening (ACSM 2015): anyone with symptoms of cardiovascular, metabolic or renal disease (chest pain, unusual breathlessness, fainting) should get medical clearance before starting. Otherwise, light-to-moderate exercise can begin and progress.

<p class="src">Source: Riebe et al., Med Sci Sports Exerc 2015 (known literature)</p>

</div>

<div class="keep" markdown="1">

**E45** (grade B (known literature)). Getting-up-from-the-floor strategies can be taught to older adults. Practice it before you ever need it (backward chaining: kneel → half-kneel → stand, using sturdy furniture).

<p class="src">Source: Hofmeyer et al., J Am Geriatr Soc 2002 (floor-rise strategy training)</p>

</div>

<div class="keep" markdown="1">

**E49** (grade A (tool/norms)). Senior Fitness Test (Rikli & Jones): 7,183 US community-dwelling adults aged 60–94 from 267 sites in 21 states. "Normal range" = the middle 50% (25th–75th percentile) for each 5-year age band and sex. 30-s chair stand, 30-s arm curl (5 lb women / 8 lb men), 2-minute step test (right-knee lifts to midway between kneecap and hip bone), chair sit-and-reach (inches, + past the toes / − short of them). Example normal ranges, women 70–74: chair stand 10–15, arm curl 12–17, step test 68–101, sit-and-reach −1.0 to +4.0 in; men 70–74: 12–17, 14–21, 80–110, −3.5 to +2.5 in. Full tables in products/strength_reset.md. It's a fitness comparison, not a diagnosis.

<p class="src">Source: Rikli & Jones, Senior Fitness Test Manual, 2nd ed. 2013 (primary not opened). Opened: normative tables — https://integrativephysicaltherapyservices.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/08/Fitness-Testing-for-Seniors-PDF.pdf ; protocol + sample size — https://fitnessnorms.com/functional/chair-sit-and-reach/ , https://fitnessnorms.com/functional/step-test/ , https://fitnessnorms.com/functional/arm-curl/ . Note: the PDF's women 60–64 sit-and-reach cell reads "−0.5 to +0.5" (typo); we use the fitnessnorms 25th–75th percentiles (−0.6 to +4.8 in).</p>

</div>
